paragraphs: A classifier’s probabilities are useful as uncertainty estimates only when they are calibrated. This paper targets canonical calibration, which evaluates the full distribution of predicted class probabilities. That is a stronger requirement than checking only the most confident label or treating each class separately. The goal is to make this demanding notion practical to estimate and incorporate into training.

The authors build a differentiable estimator using Dirichlet kernel density estimates. Its estimates converge asymptotically to the true Lp calibration error, while a geometric series correction reduces bias. For n observations, the stated computational cost is quadratic, the convergence rate is proportional to n to the power of minus one-half, and the remaining bias is of order n to the power of minus two.

The low bias makes estimation on small data subsets practical, supporting mini-batch training updates. Experiments support the estimator’s correctness and its usefulness both for measuring canonical calibration and for adding calibration penalties to learning objectives. The framework also extends to other conditional-expectation quantities, including classifier sharpness.
neurips-2022-a-consistent-and-differenti.tldr: A differentiable, low-bias estimator makes full-distribution calibration measurable and usable as a training objective.

paragraphs: Neural ILP models combine neural perception with integer linear programming, allowing a system to learn constraints while retaining a structured reasoning component. Training can be expensive when an optimization solver must run for every example in every mini-batch. This paper introduces a training strategy that avoids calling that solver during training.

The method treats the learnable cost and constraint hyperplanes as a geometric object: a polyhedron. A soft-margin loss encourages this object to separate positive examples from negative ones. Positive examples satisfy the constraints, whereas negatives violate a constraint or have an inferior cost value. Training data supply positive examples, and the authors develop methods to generate negatives. The framework accommodates both equality and inequality constraints.

Experiments cover symbolic reasoning and tasks that also involve perception. The authors report better performance and scaling than the compared neural and solver-trained approaches. In particular, the method performs well on symbolic and visual 9 by 9 Sudoku, a scale the compared Neural ILP solver could not reach. The contribution concerns removing solver calls from learning, specifically.
neurips-2022-a-solver-free-framework-for.tldr: Neural ILP models learn costs and constraints through example separation, eliminating solver calls during training and improving experimental scalability.

paragraphs: Neural cellular automata learn how a collection of cells updates its internal states. This paper brings ideas from Transformer architectures into that setting, introducing an attention mechanism that operates locally in space while maintaining a globally organized structure. The resulting model is called Vision Transformer Cellular Automata, or ViTCA.

The authors evaluate ViTCA on denoising autoencoding: learning to recover images from corrupted versions. Across six benchmark datasets, they compare it with a U-Net, a Vision Transformer, and a U-Net-based cellular automaton. With architectures configured to have similar parameter complexity, ViTCA performs better across every benchmark and on nearly every evaluation metric. That qualification matters: the reported advantage is broad, but does not cover every metric.

The paper also examines architectural variations, changes in cell states, and the model’s inductive biases. Linear probes assess information present in its converged hidden cell states. These probes achieve better results on average than those for the comparison models, suggesting that the learned states support useful representations as well as strong image reconstruction.
neurips-2022-attention-based-neural-cell.tldr: ViTCA uses localized self-attention in neural cellular automata and improves denoising and average representation-probe results in the reported comparisons.

paragraphs: This paper explains individual model decisions by asking which smallest subset of features is sufficient to preserve a prediction with high probability. Such a probabilistic sufficient explanation does not require every possible completion of the remaining features to produce the same result. Its meaning depends on the conditional probability that the prediction stays unchanged.

Estimating that probability is the central technical problem. The authors introduce a random-forest estimator designed to be accurate and fast, and establish its consistency theoretically. This estimator supports extending sufficient explanations from classification to regression. The approach also handles features that are not discrete, without requiring an explicit model of the input distribution or access to the predictive model itself.

The paper further turns these sufficient explanations into local rules for classification and regression decisions. These rules express the explanation in a form tied to an individual case. Comparisons with other explainable-AI approaches accompany the method. Its central contribution is a statistically supported way to identify compact, probabilistically sufficient explanations across both prediction settings.
neurips-2022-consistent-sufficient-expla.tldr: A consistent random-forest probability estimator supports compact sufficient explanations and local rules for classification and regression.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization chooses decisions by considering the worst cost over a specified collection of possible data distributions. In distributed settings, that objective must coexist with workers updating asynchronously, prior knowledge about the distribution, and different preferences for robustness. This paper addresses those issues for distributed optimization with non-convex objectives.

The proposed algorithm, ASPIRE, combines asynchronous gradient projection with an iterative active-set method called EASE. The authors also introduce a constrained D-norm uncertainty set. This set determines which distributions the method protects against, while incorporating a prior distribution and allowing the degree of robustness to be adjusted. The uncertainty model is therefore part of the contribution, alongside the distributed optimization procedure.

The theoretical analysis establishes convergence and studies iteration complexity. Experiments on real-world datasets report fast convergence and robustness to heterogeneous data and malicious attacks. They also show a tradeoff between robustness and performance. These findings support the framework as a way to tune protection while learning across distributed data, rather than treating the desired robustness level as fixed.
neurips-2022-distributed-distributionall.tldr: ASPIRE combines asynchronous distributed optimization with a prior-informed uncertainty set that allows robustness to be adjusted.

paragraphs: A tensor organizes data along multiple axes, and clustering such data can involve finding groups along several of those axes. This paper introduces Fused-Orth-ALS, a method that performs tensor factorization and clustering together. Its alternating least squares procedure is designed to recover an underlying compact structure while identifying the associated groups.

The theoretical results concern noisy tensors with a latent low-rank CP decomposition. Under that structure, the authors establish statistical convergence rates for both recovery and clustering. They also show that a modified alternating least squares algorithm can recover the true latent low-rank factorization for asymmetric tensors with perturbations. These guarantees are tied to the stated tensor structure rather than applying to arbitrary multidimensional data.

The paper additionally establishes clustering consistency, connecting the estimated groups to the underlying clustering in the analyzed setting. Simulations and real datasets illustrate accuracy and computational efficiency. Together, the contributions link a joint factorization-and-clustering algorithm with theoretical recovery results, giving both statistical and computational support for analyzing structured tensor data.
neurips-2022-fused-orthogonal-alternatin.tldr: Fused-Orth-ALS jointly factorizes and clusters tensors, with recovery and consistency results under stated low-rank structural assumptions.

paragraphs: Describing a video in detail requires connecting actions to their participants and tracking which entities different descriptions refer to. This paper extends video situation recognition by adding spatial and temporal grounding: associating descriptions with locations and times in the video. It addresses this richer prediction task in a weakly supervised setting.

The proposed VideoWhisperer model uses three Transformer stages. First, it learns contextual representations of video features and important objects. Next, queries about action roles gather information from object representations, localizing the relevant answers. Finally, it generates captions describing those roles. Processing a group of clips together lets the model jointly predict verbs, their roles, the nouns filling those roles, and their grounding.

On a version of VidSitu augmented with grounding information, the authors observe a large improvement in entity-caption accuracy. The model also localizes action roles without using grounding annotations during training. The result connects descriptive language with video evidence, making structured event understanding include both what an entity is doing and where the corresponding role appears.
neurips-2022-grounded-video-situation-re.tldr: VideoWhisperer jointly describes video events and grounds their participants, learning localization without grounding annotations during training.

paragraphs: When a third party trains a machine-learning model, that party may be able to embed hidden behavior while leaving the model otherwise accurate. This paper examines that supply-chain threat beyond attacks based on poisoning training data. It asks what becomes possible when an attacker directly manipulates the model’s weights.

The authors introduce handcrafted backdoors built through such direct modification. Their central argument is that weight access gives an attacker more freedom than influencing the model indirectly through poisoned examples. That broader control matters for defenses: the paper demonstrates that these attacks can effectively evade many techniques intended to detect or remove backdoors.

Across four datasets and four network architectures, the reported attack success rate remains above 96%. Those experiments support the claim that direct weight manipulation is a consequential part of the supply-chain attack space. The authors call for further research into that wider space. The findings concern the evaluated attacks and defenses; they establish a broader threat model without claiming that every backdoor defense can be defeated.
neurips-2022-handcrafted-backdoors-in-de.tldr: Direct weight manipulation enables handcrafted backdoors that evade many evaluated defenses and exceed 96% attack success in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Some modeling problems come with directional knowledge: increasing an input should only increase, or only decrease, the predicted response. This paper introduces an additive Gaussian process framework that incorporates such monotonicity constraints while scaling to many input dimensions. The authors show that its constraints hold throughout the input space.

The framework also handles more general linear inequality constraints on individual components, including componentwise convexity. To manage dimensionality, the authors propose additive MaxMod, a sequential procedure that identifies active input dimensions and refines the most important ones. It chooses updates by maximizing a squared-norm criterion that can be computed explicitly at linear cost.

This combination connects structural knowledge about the function with selective refinement of its inputs. The model can enforce its shape requirements while directing refinement toward dimensions identified as important. Demonstrations include synthetic problems with hundreds of dimensions under monotonicity constraints and a real flood application. These results provide evidence for the framework’s performance and scalability in the studied settings, alongside the guarantee that its constraints hold everywhere.
neurips-2022-high-dimensional-additive-g.tldr: An additive Gaussian process framework enforces monotonicity throughout the input space and uses sequential dimension selection to scale.

paragraphs: A generative model can produce realistic images while still representing poor underlying three-dimensional shapes. This paper argues that placing a 3D renderer inside a GAN generator gives it geometric capabilities, but does not by itself ensure good geometry. The generator learns primarily from its discriminator, so the discriminator’s supervision also matters.

The proposed GeoD framework makes that discriminator geometry-aware. Besides distinguishing real images from generated ones, it extracts geometric information from its inputs. That information then guides the generator. The approach changes what the training signal rewards, helping connect realistic two-dimensional appearance with more accurate three-dimensional structure.

Experiments across several generator architectures and training datasets report substantially improved shape accuracy and advantages over the compared state-of-the-art methods. The framework can also add novel-view synthesis as a third discriminator task, alongside real-versus-fake classification and geometry extraction. The authors report that this more capable discriminator can further improve consistency across views. The contribution is therefore a richer source of supervision for 3D-aware generation.
neurips-2022-improving-3d-aware-image-sy.tldr: GeoD improves 3D-aware image generation by asking the discriminator to extract geometry and use it to guide the generator.

paragraphs: A scene’s acoustics determine how sound changes between its source and a listener. This relationship can be represented by an impulse response for each pair of positions, which is then used to render the heard sound. Storing responses at discrete probe points can require substantial space, while geometry-based simulation can miss some wave effects.

INRAS represents these responses with a continuous neural function. Given emitter and listener positions, it produces a time-domain impulse response, allowing evaluation at arbitrary positions. The network separates its representation into features for the emitter, scene geometry, and listener. This organization allows scene-dependent features to be reused and supports training across multiple scenes and conditions.

The experiments compare representation and sound rendering as emitter and listener locations vary. The authors report improvements over existing approaches in impulse-response quality, inference speed, and storage requirements. The method’s significance is that a compact learned representation can connect continuous spatial queries to usable acoustic responses, with the reported results supporting both rendering quality and computational efficiency.
neurips-2022-inras-implicit-neural-repre.tldr: INRAS learns a compact continuous acoustic field that renders impulse responses for arbitrary emitter and listener positions.

paragraphs: Learning a dynamical system from time-series observations involves more than reproducing its usual behavior. When the system receives external inputs, its response to unexpected stimulation and noise also matters. This paper focuses on learning nonlinear input-output systems with a stability guarantee, motivated by applications such as robotics, physical modeling, and systems biology.

The method enforces stability through a differentiable projection onto a space satisfying the Hamilton-Jacobi inequality. In effect, the learned system is constrained through a mathematical condition that realizes input-output stability. Finding the projection can be expressed as a quadratically constrained quadratic programming problem, and the authors derive an analytical particular solution.

The authors apply the method to a toy bistable system and a benchmark generated by a glucose-insulin simulator. In those evaluations, their neural nonlinear systems achieve input-output stability, unlike the naive neural networks used for comparison. The contribution connects a trainable neural representation with an explicit stability mechanism, so the desired response property is built into learning rather than judged only from ordinary prediction behavior.
neurips-2022-learning-deep-input-output-.tldr: A differentiable projection enforces a mathematical stability condition while learning nonlinear input-output dynamics.

paragraphs: Spike cameras record light through continuous streams of binary events, providing very high temporal resolution. Estimating optical flow means recovering motion from those streams. This paper addresses limitations of an earlier approach that considered motion between only two moments and relied on graphics-generated training data with limited generalization.

The proposed Spike2Flow network builds a representation from differences in spike firing times together with aggregated spatial information. This combines clues about when spikes occur with information about their surrounding locations. A joint correlation decoding mechanism then uses continuous motion clues, making the ongoing stream part of the motion-estimation process.

The authors also introduce a dataset containing real-world scenes to support better generalization. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on existing synthetic datasets and on real data recorded by spike cameras. The contribution combines a representation tailored to binary spike timing, a decoder that uses continuity, and additional real-scene data. Together, these address both how motion is extracted from the sensor output and how the model is trained for real observations.
neurips-2022-learning-optical-flow-from-.tldr: Spike2Flow combines spike-timing and spatial information with continuous motion decoding, supported by a new real-world scene dataset.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes provide probabilistic function predictions, but their kernel computations can become expensive as data grows. This paper introduces a binary-tree kernel that enables regression in log-linear time in the combined number of training points and prediction locations. The kernel changes the structure of the computation by organizing data points as tree leaves.

Similarity depends only on the depth of the deepest ancestor shared by two leaves. This structure lets the kernel matrix be represented as a sum of sparse rank-one matrices, requiring linear storage and n log n construction time for n data points. The authors also give an approximate matrix inversion procedure with linear time complexity.

On a standard collection of regression tasks, the binary-tree GP achieves the highest test likelihood on more datasets than any individual alternative. It usually has lower mean squared error than sparse methods and often matches or surpasses a Matérn GP. It is fastest on the large datasets evaluated. These qualified comparisons suggest that the computational savings can coexist with competitive predictive quality.
neurips-2022-log-linear-time-gaussian-pr.tldr: A binary-tree kernel enables log-linear-time Gaussian process regression with competitive predictive performance in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Image-text matching often benefits from models trained on enormous collections of paired images and descriptions. This paper studies a different training setting: paired images and texts are unavailable. The challenge is to establish useful connections between the two kinds of information without training examples that explicitly say which image belongs with which text.

The proposed method, Multimodal Aligned Conceptual Knowledge, or MACK, uses aligned conceptual knowledge to correlate images and language. Inspired by human knowledge use, it can serve directly as general knowledge without additional model training. It can also be fine-tuned using unpaired images and texts to better adapt to particular datasets.

The authors further extend MACK into a re-ranking method that can be combined with existing image-text matching models. They report substantial performance improvements from that combination. The contribution therefore offers several uses for the same conceptual knowledge: direct matching, adaptation without paired examples, and refinement of another model’s rankings. Its importance lies in broadening the available training setup for connecting visual and textual content.
neurips-2022-mack-multimodal-aligned-con.tldr: MACK uses aligned conceptual knowledge to match images and text without paired training examples and to improve existing models through re-ranking.

paragraphs: Combining several camera views can help reconstruct a person’s three-dimensional pose and body shape, but many methods require known camera parameters. That requirement restricts their use with sources such as social videos. This paper aligns views using the shared human body itself, removing the need for spatial camera calibration.

The method uses dense body correspondences to map image features onto a common body-surface coordinate system that is independent of viewpoint and pose. Features from different images can then be combined according to which body locations they describe. A learned self-attention mechanism assesses confidence within and across views, and a regressor uses the fused features to predict body-model parameters.

The authors report reliable pose and shape reconstruction, outperforming single-view methods whose results are combined afterward. The advantage is especially apparent when substantial occlusion hides parts of the body. Accuracy is also comparable to multiview methods that require calibration. These findings support semantic correspondence as a useful basis for combining views when camera geometry is unavailable.
neurips-2022-multiview-human-body-recons.tldr: Mapping image features onto a shared body surface enables multiview human reconstruction without camera calibration.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization nests one optimization problem inside another: the upper objective depends on a solution produced by the lower problem. If the lower problem is non-convex, it may have several critical points. Without specifying which one is selected, the upper problem can be ambiguous because different lower-level outcomes can lead to different decisions.

This paper introduces selection maps that specify a particular lower-level solution. Using these maps, the authors define hierarchical games between two agents. They develop analytical tools from Morse theory to extend implicit differentiation, establishing its validity even in the presence of degenerate critical points where the usual implicit function theorem cannot be applied.

The paper also connects this formulation to algorithms that differentiate through a finite sequence of optimization steps. It shows that such unrolled algorithms solve the proposed games up to approximation errors arising from finite computation. The authors then propose a simple correction to remove those errors. The contribution clarifies both which problem these algorithms address and how their approximate computations relate to it.
neurips-2022-non-convex-bilevel-games-wi.tldr: Selection maps resolve ambiguity in non-convex bilevel problems and support extended differentiation theory and corrected unrolled algorithms.

paragraphs: Non-autoregressive translation produces outputs without the usual word-by-word generation process. Its training can nevertheless be sensitive to exact word positions: cross-entropy heavily penalizes even small shifts. CTC-based latent alignment relaxes that restriction, but its order-preserving alignments still cannot accommodate the global word reordering that often occurs in translation.

This paper expands the possible alignments to include non-monotonic ones, allowing words to match without preserving their order. It also considers alignments that overlap with the target sentence. The model is trained to maximize the F1 score of this non-monotonic matching, changing how candidate alignments receive credit during learning.

Experiments on major WMT benchmarks show substantial improvements over CTC-based translation models. The best reported system reaches 30.06 BLEU on WMT14 English-to-German using a single decoding iteration. The authors describe this as narrowing the performance gap between non-autoregressive and autoregressive models. The result supports a more flexible training alignment as a way to improve translation while retaining one-iteration decoding.
neurips-2022-non-monotonic-latent-alignm.tldr: Allowing non-monotonic latent alignments improves CTC-based translation while retaining single-iteration decoding.

paragraphs: Online convex optimization evaluates a sequence of decisions by comparing its cumulative loss with that of a fixed comparator. This paper develops parameter-free algorithms for unbounded decision domains when only potentially heavy-tailed subgradient estimates are available. It aims for high-probability regret guarantees, extending beyond earlier results that controlled expected regret under sub-exponential subgradients.

The unbounded domain creates a specific analytical obstacle: the algorithm can produce exponentially large iterates. Consequently, the straightforward martingale concentration arguments available in bounded settings do not suffice. The authors introduce new regularization techniques to address this difficulty and support their regret analysis under weaker assumptions on the subgradient estimates.

The stated moment assumption requires a bounded pth moment for some p greater than one and at most two. The reported regret expression scales with the comparator norm and T to the power of one over p, together with logarithmic factors involving the confidence parameter. This makes the relationship between the moment assumption and the time dependence explicit: the bound changes with the available degree of tail control.
neurips-2022-parameter-free-regret-in-hi.tldr: New regularization techniques support parameter-free online optimization with high-probability regret guarantees under heavy-tailed subgradient estimates.

paragraphs: A decision policy can affect the environment in ways that change future outcomes and fairness. Rules that work well in a static setting may therefore struggle when applied repeatedly. This paper studies long-term fairness through Markov decision processes, which represent decisions and their consequences in dynamically changing environments.

The authors use deep reinforcement learning to optimize policies and introduce fairness requirements through advantage regularization. Advantage evaluations assess the relative appeal of different actions; regularizing them makes fairness part of the policy update process. The proposed methods allow fairness constraints to be imposed without engineering a new reward or sacrificing training efficiency.

The paper reports that policy optimization can find strictly better policies than previously known strategies, often achieving both higher overall utility and fewer fairness violations. Detailed analyses cover incident-monitoring attention allocation, bank loan approval, and vaccine distribution in population networks. These results support learning policies with long-term consequences in view, while preserving the qualification that simultaneous gains in utility and fairness occur often rather than universally.
neurips-2022-policy-optimization-with-ad.tldr: Regularizing action advantages incorporates long-term fairness into policy optimization and often improves both utility and fairness in the studied settings.

paragraphs: Federated learning keeps users’ training data local, but transmitted gradients can still expose information about those data. This paper introduces FILM, an attack that reconstructs private text from language-model gradients. It demonstrates that text recovery can remain feasible even when gradients come from batches containing up to 128 sentences.

FILM first identifies a set of words from the gradients, then reconstructs sentences through beam search and a prior-based reordering strategy. Across several large-scale datasets, the authors report high-fidelity recovery of individual sentences from large batches. Applying the attack iteratively can also recover multiple sentences. These results show that batching alone does not eliminate the demonstrated leakage.

The authors evaluate gradient pruning, differentially private stochastic gradient descent, and freezing word embeddings. In their evaluations, the first two substantially reduce utility. When fine-tuning a public pretrained language model on private text, keeping word embeddings fixed effectively defends against FILM with minimal utility loss. That defense result is specific to the stated fine-tuning setup and evaluated attack.
neurips-2022-recovering-private-text-in-.tldr: FILM recovers private text from federated language-model gradients, while frozen word embeddings provide an effective evaluated defense during fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Partial-label learning gives each training example several candidate labels instead of a single confirmed answer. The learner must determine which candidate is correct. This paper examines what happens when that ambiguity is combined with a long-tailed class distribution, where classes occur at very different frequencies. Methods developed around balanced classes can perform poorly in this combined setting.

The authors propose SoLar, an optimal-transport framework that refines the labels inferred during disambiguation. Its refinement encourages the overall label distribution to match the marginal class prior. Because that prior must be determined under ambiguous labeling, SoLar also includes a systematic mechanism for estimating the long-tailed class distribution within the partial-label setting.

Experiments on standardized benchmarks show substantially better results than the compared state-of-the-art partial-label methods. The approach matters because label disambiguation and class frequency are handled together: the method adjusts inferred labels using an estimated distribution that reflects imbalance. The reported findings support this combination for learning when examples have both uncertain labels and uneven class representation.
neurips-2022-solar-sinkhorn-label-refine.tldr: SoLar uses optimal transport and class-prior estimation to refine ambiguous labels when classes are imbalanced.

paragraphs: Predicting atomic energies and forces is central to computational chemistry, but traditional density-functional calculations are expensive. This paper introduces the Spherical Channel Network as a learned model for those quantities. It represents an atomic system as a graph, with atoms as nodes and connections linking neighboring atoms.

Each atom’s representation contains spherical functions, called spherical channels, expressed using spherical harmonics. The network rotates these representations according to the three-dimensional orientation of each edge. The authors show that this can allow messages to use more information while retaining rotational equivariance, meaning their transformation remains consistent with rotation.

The paper also investigates relaxing equivariance in message passing and aggregation. Although equivariance is desirable, the authors find that loosening it can improve accuracy. On the large Open Catalyst 2020 dataset, the network achieves state-of-the-art energy and force prediction across numerous tasks and metrics. The findings connect a direction-sensitive representation with strong empirical performance, while showing that strict enforcement of the symmetry is not always the most accurate choice in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2022-spherical-channels-for-mode.tldr: Spherical Channel Networks use orientation-aware atomic representations to achieve strong energy and force predictions, with accuracy gains possible from relaxed equivariance.

paragraphs: Connecting what an object looks like with how it feels is useful for tasks involving physical interaction. This paper introduces Touch and Go, a dataset pairing visual and tactile observations collected by people in natural environments. Collectors touch objects with tactile sensors while recording video from their own viewpoint.

The collection includes a wide range of objects and scenes outside the laboratory and simulation settings that dominated earlier efforts. Recording sight and touch together provides paired observations of the same physical interactions. This makes the dataset useful for studying how models can connect information across these two sensory channels.

The authors demonstrate three applications. Self-supervised learning builds visual and tactile features from the paired data. Tactile-driven image stylization changes an object’s appearance to better match a supplied touch signal. A prediction task uses combined visual and tactile inputs to forecast future tactile frames. Successful applications across these tasks show that the dataset supports learning shared representations, modifying visual appearance, and predicting the progression of tactile observations.
neurips-2022-touch-and-go-learning-from-.tldr: Touch and Go pairs human-collected video and touch data from natural environments for multimodal learning and prediction.

paragraphs: Frequency-domain models can capture long-range relationships in space and time using compact spectral descriptions. Existing designs often alternate between spectral and input-space computation, requiring forward and inverse Fourier transforms at every layer. This paper introduces Transform Once, or T1, which removes redundant transformations by learning directly in the frequency domain after a single transform.

To support that design, the authors derive a weight initialization scheme that preserves variance and investigate how to select frequencies for reduced-order models. These components address how the network begins learning and which spectral information it retains. The resulting blueprint simplifies frequency-domain model design while reducing computational overhead.

Experiments learn solution operators for spatiotemporal dynamics, including incompressible Navier-Stokes systems, turbulent airfoil flows, and high-resolution smoke video. The authors report speedups from 3 to 10 times, increasing with resolution and model size, alongside predictive-error reductions exceeding 20% across tasks. Their large-scale experiment takes 5 hours instead of 32. In these evaluations, eliminating repeated transforms improves both computational efficiency and test performance.
neurips-2022-transform-once-efficient-op.tldr: Transform Once learns directly in frequency space, reducing repeated-transform costs while improving accuracy in the reported dynamics experiments.
